Instead, this version ensures that any attempt to use the package results in an immediate and unrecoverable error, violating the trust and expectations of downstream users.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A package might throw an error if a critical dependency is missing, if the environment is unsupported, or if the user is using a deprecated API. However, it is not legitimate for a widely used package to throw an error unconditionally for all consumers, as this constitutes a denial of service.
key_indicators: Main entry point (index.js) contains only an error-throwing statement
Complete removal of all functional code from the package
Error is thrown immediately upon import, with no conditional logic
No legitimate functionality or exports are provided

package_info.why_malicious: The faker@6.6.6 package was intentionally sabotaged by its maintainer as a form of protestware. In this version, all original source code was removed and replaced with a single statement that throws an error immediately upon import. This deliberate action causes any project that installs or upgrades to this version to fail at runtime, resulting in a denial-of-service condition for all dependent applications and pipelines. The package is therefore malicious at the macro level due to its intentional disruption of the software supply chain.

attack_chain.action: Maintainer publishes a new major version (6.6.6) of faker with all original source code removed and replaced by code that throws an error immediately upon import.
attack_chain.leads_to: Any project that upgrades to or installs faker@6.6.6 will immediately fail at runtime due to the thrown error.

attack_chain.action: Consumers of the package experience denial of service as their applications, build pipelines, or test suites fail to start or execute.
attack_chain.leads_to: Disruption of development workflows and production systems that rely on faker, potentially causing widespread outages and productivity loss.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for major version updates of critical dependencies that remove all or most source code, especially if the main entry point throws an error or disables all functionality. Automated dependency analysis tools should flag packages where the main export is a function that only throws, or where the package contents are drastically reduced compared to previous versions. Review changelogs and diffs for sudden, unexplained code removal and error-throwing logic in the main entry point.

malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A package might be deprecated with a warning or error, but not by removing all functionality and breaking all consumers without notice.
